title: Context Caching (Anthropic/OpenAI Feature)
summary: Reuse provider-supported computation for stable prompt prefixes while preserving fresh generation and provider-specific eligibility, retention, and billing rules.
overview: Context caching, often called prompt or prefix caching, reuses intermediate computation for an eligible repeated prefix. The provider still generates a new response for the request. It differs from semantic caching, which returns a previously generated answer for a similar question, and from durable agent memory, which stores application state.

OpenAI and Anthropic expose provider- and model-specific caching behavior. Eligibility thresholds, prefix matching, controls, retention, routing, and usage accounting can differ and change over time. OpenAI documents model-dependent cache controls and reporting; Anthropic documents explicit and automatic caching options with cache-control semantics. Verify the exact model and deployment documentation instead of assuming one provider’s parameters or lifetime apply to another.

production.poc: A prototype repeats identical stable prefixes and confirms reuse through reported usage rather than latency alone.
production.production: Production uses deterministic prompt serialization, separates stable from changing segments, and records cache read, write, and miss behavior.
production.scale: Enterprise scale evaluates retention and data policies, request locality, template-version churn, and net economics including any cache-write charges.

components.name: Stable prefix builder
components.role: Serializes reusable instructions, tool definitions, and approved reference material consistently.

components.name: Provider cache adapter
components.role: Applies the supported model-specific controls without pretending all providers share one API.

components.name: Dynamic suffix assembler
components.role: Appends changing user data and current task evidence after reusable segments where appropriate.

components.name: Usage collector
components.role: Records provider-reported cached usage and relevant billing categories.

components.name: Cache effectiveness monitor
components.role: Tracks reuse, prefix changes, retention behavior, and total accepted-task cost.

flow.title: Check provider eligibility
flow.description: Verify supported model, prefix requirements, controls, and applicable data-retention policy.

flow.title: Identify reusable content
flow.description: Separate stable instructions and schemas from timestamps, user-specific facts, and changing retrieval.

flow.title: Serialize consistently
flow.description: Keep segment order and bytes stable where the provider requires matching prefixes.

flow.title: Apply supported controls
flow.description: Use the provider’s documented caching mechanism and version the adapter configuration.

flow.title: Submit a fresh request
flow.description: Send the dynamic suffix and treat the output as a new generation requiring normal validation.

flow.title: Measure actual reuse
flow.description: Inspect reported usage and compare net cost and latency with a no-reuse baseline.

useCase.title: Repeated analysis with a stable schema catalog
useCase.situation: An analytics assistant uses a large approved schema description across many separate questions.
useCase.problem: The same schema instructions are repeatedly processed, but timestamps inserted near the beginning prevent prefix reuse.
useCase.requirement: Reduce repeated prefill work while keeping each query’s data and answer current.
useCase.architecture: A deterministic prefix contains the versioned schema and tool definitions; current task data appears in a separate suffix.
runtime: Requests sharing the same approved schema revision become eligible for provider reuse.
Usage records confirm whether cache reads occurred and whether overall cost improved.
useCase.failure: When the schema changes, the prefix version changes intentionally; correctness takes priority over retaining the previous cache hit rate.
useCase.impact: Measure cached-token share, write and read cost, time to first output, and template churn; a warm prefix is an optimization, not an availability guarantee.

tradeoffs.cost: May retain unnecessary context if optimized without task relevance.

tradeoffs.benefit: Can improve reuse across wider intervals.
tradeoffs.cost: May change cost and data-policy implications.
Must preserve real capability differences instead of hiding them.

failures.detection: Reported cache reuse remains low despite repeated tasks.
failures.recovery: Remove unnecessary volatile fields from the reusable prefix.

failures.detection: Expected hits become misses under the selected model.
failures.recovery: Verify current retention semantics and size capacity for misses.

mistakes.mistake: Treating caching as semantic answer reuse
mistakes.fix: Keep normal generation and output validation.

mistakes.mistake: Assuming cache hits from faster latency
mistakes.fix: Inspect documented usage fields and reconcile cost.

whenToUse: Use for repeated stable instructions and tool schemas.
Use for recurring work over the same approved reference prefix.
Use when provider-reported reuse yields net benefit.
whenNotToUse: Avoid adding irrelevant text merely to increase cached tokens.
Do not assume cached content is durable memory.
Avoid retention settings incompatible with the data policy.
checklist: Verify the exact provider and model contract.
Record cache read and write usage.
Benchmark misses and reconcile net cost.
